request.prompt: [quiet, stunned] Ollie. [long pause] [quiet, breaking] You've been here the whole time. Under the chapel. [long pause] [quiet, guilty] The one place you promised you never would. I said best spot ever.
[quiet, tender] Your sneakers, side by side. Your flashlight. A comic. [long pause] [quiet, heartbroken] You made it nice in here. You thought I was coming.
[quiet, heartbroken] You made it nice in here. You thought I was coming.

[quiet, matter-of-fact] A scratch in the stone for every count. A hundred to a block. [long pause] [quiet] When I didn't come, you gave me another hundred. And another. Six hundred and fifty-seven. [long pause] [quiet, slow] Then the counting stops. Ten to ten. That's when the knocking starts. [long pause] [quiet, breaking] That's the minute you gave up on me.

[quiet, tired, intimate] You hid where I told you. The stone shut behind you. Nobody came. [long pause] [quiet, tender] So you took your shoes off. Folded your sheet for a pillow, and pulled the rest of it over you. [long pause] [quiet, breaking] You went to sleep waiting, and you never woke up. You were seven.
[quiet, rueful] It was your whole plan for the night. Hide and seek with me. [long pause] [quiet, ashamed] I gave it to you to get rid of you.
[softly, matter-of-fact] Fifty-seven. You left me forty-three.

[quiet, gentle] I brought your candy. From all the houses. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] June's candy apple. You never ate yours. You just carried it. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] Mrs. K's full-size bar. Stop two, every year. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] Frank's peanuts. Save half for Bo. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] The twins' popcorn ball. For whoever hid the longest. That's you. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] A sheriff's star, for your coat. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] A peppermint. You practised. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] Nonna's cannoli. She made you a plate every year. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] A pouch, from a kid who never met you. [long pause] [quiet, proud] Your dare candy. You did it. Everybody's going to know. [long pause] [quiet, ashamed] Nothing from the Deckers'. That one's on me.
[quiet, gentle] And your map. I walked all of it.
[quiet, steady] I'm not moving you. You stay here tonight, under your sheet. [long pause] [quiet, resolved] In the morning I tell them where you are. Tonight I carry your bag.
[quiet, warm] You're behind me. Three steps back, same as always. [long pause] [quiet, rueful] I used to walk faster so you'd have to run. [long pause] [softly] Not tonight.
[straining, quiet] It takes everything I have to shift this stone. You were seven.
[quiet, tired] It takes everything I have to shift this stone. You were seven.

[quiet] Twenty-nine red glasses, burnt down. One place left. [long pause] [quiet, tender] Mom lit one here every Halloween. To the saint of lost things. [long pause] [quiet, breaking] She was standing right on top of you.
[quiet, intimate] Here's this year's, Mom. I found him.

[quiet, tired, honest] I was sixteen. I wanted one night without you. [long pause] [quiet, honest] That's all it was. There isn't a bigger reason. [long pause] [quiet] You did everything I ever told you to. [long pause] [quiet, bitter] "Next week," she wrote. "Next year," he wrote. Everybody was going to get to you later. [long pause] [quiet, breaking] I'm sorry, Ollie.
[quiet, surrendering] I give up, Ollie. You win.
[softly, calling] Game's over. You can come out now. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] Go on home. I'm right behind you. [long pause] [quiet] They're going out behind you. You don't need them now.
[quiet, remembering] One year I waited at a gate. [long pause] [quiet, tender] This year you waited.

[quiet, wondering] A tall one and a small one. You drew this. [long pause] [quiet, gentle] That's our porch. Go on in. [long pause] [quiet, tired, intimate] Twenty-nine of them, Mom. That makes thirty.
